# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence reviewed
Single artifact in the evidence directory: `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (15,512 frames, 6.3 MB, capture duration ~15,689 sec / 4.4 hrs). No IDS/Suricata alert export or other artifacts were present alongside the capture.

## Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 | Conversation stats, all identity queries below |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.2.28.88`), confirmed same MAC in DHCP request |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR | DHCP option 12 hostname; corroborated by NBNS `DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR<00>/<20>` |
| Windows domain | EASYAS123 (easyas123.tech) | NBNS workgroup/browser records; DNS queries for `EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech` |
| Logged-in user | brolf | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.2.28.88 and the DC (10.2.28.2) |

LAN scope: /24 on 10.2.28.0, gateway/DC at 10.2.28.2 (Local Master Browser `EASYAS123`, LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP target). 10.2.28.88 is the only host generating the suspicious traffic below.

## Malware family
**NetSupport RAT** (the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client abused as a commodity RAT). **Attribution: behavioral**, based on literal protocol strings observed in the traffic itself — no IDS alert file was provided to give a signature match, but the client identifies itself by name in every request:

- Client: `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`
- Server banner: `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`
- Protocol: repeating `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` beacons answered with `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<encrypted blob>`, all carried as plaintext HTTP (not TLS) over destination port 443 — a known NetSupport RAT trick to blend in with normal HTTPS port usage while avoiding a real TLS handshake.

This traffic is confined entirely to TCP stream 40 between 10.2.28.88:51912 and 45.131.214.85:443, and recurs roughly 260+ times over the full capture window, i.e. persistent C2 beaconing/tasking, not a one-off connection.

No malware binary/dropper was observed being transferred over HTTP in this capture (the only application/octet-stream-class downloads present are legitimate Chrome extension CRX updates and Windows Update CAB files, both to Microsoft/Akamai CDN infrastructure — benign). The infection therefore predates the start of this capture; delivery vector cannot be established from this evidence alone.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | 45.131.214.85:443 (TCP) | tcp.stream 40, sustained NetSupport POLL/ENCD exchange, `10.2.28.88 <-> 45.131.214.85` conversation (823+445 frames) |
| Domain | vadusa.xyz | `dns.qry.name==vadusa.xyz`, frame 2566, resolves A record to 45.131.214.85 |
| URL | http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm | Repeated `POST` requests, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, frames 2638–15499 (260+ occurrences) |

No file names or file hashes could be grounded — no executable/binary transfer for this malware is present in the capture; nothing to hash.

## Benign context (not indicators)
- Microsoft/Windows Update, OCSP (DigiCert), Adobe ARM check, Chrome extension CRX delivery via `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, MSN/Bing telemetry, NVIDIA GFE, Google API update pings — all standard OS/app background noise to Microsoft/Akamai/Google infrastructure.
- 23.64.147.24, 23.218.232.148, 150.171.x.x, 20.42.x.x, 52.x.x.x — Microsoft/Akamai cloud ranges tied to the above services, not attacker infrastructure.
- Internal AD/domain traffic (LDAP, Kerberos, DRSUAPI, SAMR, LSARPC, NBNS, CLDAP) between 10.2.28.88 and 10.2.28.2 — normal domain-joined workstation behavior.

## Summary
Windows workstation **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), domain EASYAS123, logged in as user **brolf**, is compromised with **NetSupport RAT** (behavioral attribution via NetSupport Manager/Gateway protocol strings — no signature/IDS confirmation available). The implant beacons persistently throughout the entire ~4.4-hour capture to **45.131.214.85:443** (domain **vadusa.xyz**) via `POST /fakeurl.htm`, exchanging encrypted `CMD=ENCD` tasking data consistent with active remote-control/C2 usage. No dropper or additional payload transfer is visible in this capture, so the initial infection vector predates the capture window.
